pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In the family tree in the lesson, Amina's father's sister is her (1 mark)
   A. cousin
   B. aunt
   C. sibling
   D. grandmother

2. Articles: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. She has an uncle.
   B. She has uncle an.
   C. She has the an uncle.
   D. She has a uncle.

3. What should you do if a question does not apply to you? (1 mark)
   A. Write a false answer
   B. Leave it empty
   C. Tear the form
   D. Write N/A or draw a line

4. Which word means a very big and special meal? (1 mark)
   A. snack
   B. chore
   C. ribbon
   D. feast

5. Poems and similes: Which sentence has a simile? (1 mark)
   A. The runner was tired.
   B. The runner was as fast as a cheetah.
   C. The runner won the race.
   D. The race started at nine.

6. What is the plural of 'church'? (1 mark)
   A. churchs
   B. churchies
   C. churches
   D. churchen

7. Which part of a composition tells who, where and when? (1 mark)
   A. The title only
   B. The conclusion
   C. The body
   D. The introduction

8. Which phrase do we use to get someone's attention politely? (1 mark)
   A. Give me
   B. Excuse me
   C. Hey you
   D. Move away

9. 'She sighed with relief' means she (1 mark)
   A. was happy that a worry was over
   B. was very tired
   C. was very angry
   D. was afraid

10. In 'bandage', the stress is on (1 mark)
   A. both syllables
   B. the first syllable
   C. the second syllable
   D. neither

11. Which word starts with the cluster 'sn'? (1 mark)
   A. snake
   B. stitch
   C. stop
   D. treatment

12. Which is better for sharing a lot of news and feelings? (1 mark)
   A. A one-word SMS
   B. A phone number
   C. A signature
   D. A letter

13. Which date form is correct in a letter? (1 mark)
   A. 14th May 2026
   B. 2026 May 14
   C. 14 2026 May
   D. May 2026 14th

14. Which word fits: 'Do you have ___ pencils?' (1 mark)
   A. much
   B. some
   C. a lot
   D. any

15. Which quantifier goes with an uncountable noun in a question? (1 mark)
   A. much
   B. many
   C. few
   D. several

16. How long should a Grade 4 pictorial composition be? (1 mark)
   A. 500 words
   B. 5 words
   C. 20 words
   D. about 60 to 80 words

17. What is turn-taking in a conversation? (1 mark)
   A. Both people speak at the same time
   B. One person speaks all the time
   C. Only the teacher speaks
   D. One person speaks while the other listens, then they swap

18. Which word means 'free time when you rest or play'? (1 mark)
   A. crime
   B. trust
   C. leisure
   D. laptop

19. What does the proverb 'Look before you leap' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Jump as high as you can
   B. Think carefully before you act
   C. Always look at your feet
   D. Do not go outside

20. Which word begins with /w/? (1 mark)
   A. very
   B. water
   C. vet
   D. van

21. Why is fast reading not always good reading? (1 mark)
   A. Speed is never important
   B. Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again
   C. Fast readers cannot use their eyes
   D. Books are meant to be read slowly only

22. What is the short form of 'let us'? (1 mark)
   A. let's
   B. let'us
   C. lets'
   D. le'ts

23. Which of these can spread HIV? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing a razor blade
   B. Playing football together
   C. Sharing a plate of food
   D. Hugging a friend

24. Which question is factual? (1 mark)
   A. How did Omondi feel deep inside?
   B. Why do you think Baraka is brave?
   C. What lesson does the story teach?
   D. Who told Baraka about how HIV spreads?

25. Which adverb of frequency completes: 'I ____ wash my hands before eating.' (every time)? (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. always
   C. rarely
   D. seldom

26. How does your voice usually change at the end of a question? (1 mark)
   A. It stays flat
   B. It becomes silent
   C. It goes down
   D. It goes up

27. Which sentence has a comma used correctly before 'but'? (1 mark)
   A. I, wanted to go but it was raining.
   B. I wanted to go but, it was raining.
   C. I wanted to go, but it was raining.
   D. I wanted, to go but it was raining.

28. What does 'sanitation' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A type of shoe
   B. A game
   C. Clean toilets, drains and waste systems that protect health
   D. A kind of food

29. What does 'rinse' mean? (1 mark)
   A. To make dirty
   B. To cook
   C. To dry with cloth
   D. To wash with clean water to take off soap

30. Which is an opinion, not a fact? (1 mark)
   A. Germs are too small to see.
   B. Cold water is the nicest to drink.
   C. Soap helps to remove germs.
   D. Boiled water is safer than untreated river water.

31. Which is a main idea of the text 'Keeping Clean to Stay Healthy'? (1 mark)
   A. Germs are good for us
   B. Flies help us
   C. Good hygiene keeps us healthy
   D. Soap is expensive

32. Which is NOT one of the five senses? (1 mark)
   A. sleep
   B. taste
   C. smell
   D. sight

33. Which word begins with the cluster 'cl'? (1 mark)
   A. green
   B. print
   C. brush
   D. clean

34. In 'The Clean-Up Day', which proverb did Kamau use about fixing the hole in the fence? (1 mark)
   A. Many hands make light work
   B. Look before you leap
   C. Prevention is better than cure
   D. A stitch in time saves nine

35. What is the past participle of 'eat'? (1 mark)
   A. eaten
   B. ate
   C. eated
   D. eating

36. Which sentence uses the correct participle of 'eat'? (1 mark)
   A. She has ate her lunch.
   B. She have eaten her lunch.
   C. She has eaten her lunch.
   D. She has eating her lunch.

37. Which word can help you show the order of events in a diary? (1 mark)
   A. then
   B. broom
   C. green
   D. desk

38. What is a good way to end a diary entry? (1 mark)
   A. With a poem only
   B. With a map
   C. With a plan for tomorrow or a short sign-off
   D. With a list of prices

39. What is an advertisement? (1 mark)
   A. A news story
   B. A weather report
   C. A letter to the editor
   D. A notice that tries to sell something

40. Which preposition completes: 'The bank is ____ the school and the post office.'? (1 mark)
   A. through
   B. among
   C. between
   D. into

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the difference between 'I have eaten' and 'I had eaten when he came.' (3 marks)

42. Give one riddle about an object used for cleaning, with its answer. (2 marks)

43. Explain why gestures should match your words. (2 marks)

44. Give two pieces of advice for staying safe online. (3 marks)

45. Put in order: Baraka presses Send; Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose. (3 marks)

46. Write the steps you would follow to search for information safely online. (4 marks)

47. Give two things you can add to a pictorial composition that are not in the pictures. (2 marks)

48. Give two words with /θ/ and two with /ð/. (4 marks)

49. List three details that a school library form may ask for. (3 marks)

50. Give directions from your classroom to the school gate using at least three prepositions. (3 marks)

51. Write one sentence in the present progressive and one in the past progressive about a farm. (4 marks)

52. Fill in with a, an or the: 'Mama bought ___ cabbage and ___ egg. ___ egg was big.' (3 marks)

53. Write a or an before each word: egg, banana, umbrella, hour. (2 marks)

54. Why is it important to use polite words? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

55. Write three sentences using three of these words: because, different, address, favourite, tomorrow. (3 marks)

56. Give a memory trick for spelling 'necessary' or 'separate'. (2 marks)

57. Mark the words you would stress in: 'We must keep our compound clean.' (3 marks)

58. Write three yes/no questions about keeping the compound clean. (3 marks)

59. Explain why flies are dangerous to health. (2 marks)

60. Arrange in alphabetical order: goat, cow, hen, dog. (2 marks)

61. List three things that make handwriting legible. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — aunt
   A father's sister is an aunt.

2. A — She has an uncle.
   Uncle starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.

3. D — Write N/A or draw a line
   N/A means not applicable and shows that you did not forget.

4. D — feast
   A feast is a large special meal.

5. B — The runner was as fast as a cheetah.
   It compares the runner with a cheetah using as ... as.

6. C — churches
   Nouns ending in ch add es.

7. D — The introduction
   The introduction sets the scene.

8. B — Excuse me
   Excuse me is polite.

9. A — was happy that a worry was over
   Relief is the feeling when a worry ends.

10. B — the first syllable
   We say BAN-dage.

11. A — snake
   Snake starts with s and n.

12. D — A letter
   A letter can hold more news.

13. A — 14th May 2026
   The usual order is day, month, year.

14. D — any
   Any is used in questions with plural nouns.

15. A — much
   How much water?

16. D — about 60 to 80 words
   The design asks for about 60 to 80 words.

17. D — One person speaks while the other listens, then they swap
   In turn-taking each speaker waits for the other to finish before speaking.

18. C — leisure
   Leisure is free time.

19. B — Think carefully before you act
   It advises us to think before we do something.

20. B — water
   'Water' begins with /w/, said with rounded lips.

21. B — Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again
   Rushing causes errors that hurt understanding.

22. A — let's
   The apostrophe replaces the u.

23. A — Sharing a razor blade
   HIV can pass through blood, so razor blades must never be shared.

24. D — Who told Baraka about how HIV spreads?
   A factual question has its answer stated in the text.

25. B — always
   'Always' means every time.

26. D — It goes up
   A question ends with a rising voice.

27. C — I wanted to go, but it was raining.
   A comma comes before but when joining two full sentences.

28. C — Clean toilets, drains and waste systems that protect health
   Sanitation protects health by keeping waste away.

29. D — To wash with clean water to take off soap
   You rinse after using soap.

30. B — Cold water is the nicest to drink.
   An opinion says what someone thinks.

31. C — Good hygiene keeps us healthy
   The whole text supports good hygiene.

32. A — sleep
   The senses are sight, sound, smell, touch and taste.

33. D — clean
   'Clean' begins with c and l.

34. D — A stitch in time saves nine
   He wanted to fix the small hole before it got worse.

35. A — eaten
   Eat, ate, eaten.

36. C — She has eaten her lunch.
   Has + eaten.

37. A — then
   'Then' is a time word.

38. C — With a plan for tomorrow or a short sign-off
   Diaries often end with plans or 'Goodnight'.

39. D — A notice that tries to sell something
   Adverts try to sell.

40. C — between
   'Between' is used for two things.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'I have eaten' says the eating is finished and it matters now. 'I had eaten when he came' says I finished eating before he came, in the past.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for the time link.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have hairs but no head, and I clean your teeth. What am I? A toothbrush.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a clear riddle and 1 for the correct answer.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: If they do not match, the listener may be confused about what you mean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for confusion and 1 for a clear reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not give your name, school or address to strangers. Show worrying messages to a trusted adult. Ask a parent or teacher before opening a new page.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct piece of advice, up to 3.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Achieng explains what an email is; they click Compose; Baraka presses Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what to find out; choose key words; use an approved site; read carefully and note the facts in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: What people say, and how people feel or think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: /θ/: think, three, thank, mouth (any two). /ð/: this, that, the, mother (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, grade, date of birth, school name, address, class teacher, head teacher (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Go out of the classroom, walk along the corridor and go past the office to the gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct preposition.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The farmer is digging the field. The cows were eating grass.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence: 1 for the correct form of be, 1 for the -ing verb.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: a, an, The
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct article.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: an egg, a banana, an umbrella, an hour
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each correct answer.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polite words show respect and make people feel welcome. They help people to cooperate and be friendly.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences using the words with correct spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: 'Necessary' has one collar (c) and two sleeves (ss); 'separate' has 'a rat' in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a trick and 1 for a correct explanation.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: We must KEEP our COMpound CLEAN. (Important words: keep, compound, clean.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each important word.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Do you sweep the compound? Is the bin covered? Can we plant a tree?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Flies land on waste and then on food, so they carry germs to the food we eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste then food and 1 mark for germs spreading.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: cow, dog, goat, hen
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for c and d first, 1 mark for g and h last.

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters of the correct size, letters sitting on the line, even gaps between letters and words, correct spelling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
